pages.text:
WFP Timor-Leste 2021 Annual Country Report highlights
FUNDING
SCHOOL HEALTH AND NUTRITION
3,000 students benefitted from school health and nutrition pilot projects in Dili municipality
BEHAVIOUR CHANGE COMMUNICATION
SAVINGLIVESCHANGINGLIVES
US$ 7.9 Millionreceived in 202175% of the country strategic plan funded
120 nutrition clubsreceived communication materials on benefits of healthy eating habit
176,000 people reached through a national television campaign on nutrition 113,891 people reached through social media with nutrition and healthy eating messages

EMERGENCY RESPONSE
50 people living with disabilities received take-home rations
ADVOCACY
11,000 pregnant and breastfeeding women reached with high-energy biscuits to prevent malnutrition through supporting the Ministry of Health 441 students provided with take-home rations and COVID-19 protection gear during school closures496 MT of relief items transported on behalf of 7 organizations post Cyclone Seroja9 UNHAS flights transported relief items, including vaccines, and 888 personnel during COVID-19 border closures
Supported Timor-Leste’s participation in the UN Food Systems Summit
Timor-Leste joined Global School Meals Coalition
Provided technical support to the government on SDG2 Consolidated National Action Plan for Nutrition Food Security (CNAP-NFS)

CAPACITY STRENGTHENING
117 health workers trained on treatment of acute malnutrition for pregnant and breastfeeding mothers and children
A blending machine installed in Tibar toboost local production of fortified rice
Food Safety Guidelinefor Safer School Meals in Timor-Leste developed and handed over to the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports
DONORS
European UnionCivil Protection andHumanitarian AID
Fromthe people of Japan
Republic of KoreaPortugal
Timor-Leste
125 government officials trained on conducting rapidassessments and data collection on impact of Cyclone Seroja
294 stakeholders participated in consultations in food fortification law and introduction of fortified rice in national social safety net programmes
6 mobile data collection tools introduced during COVID-19 and Cyclone Seroja to support the government response
Supported the government’s blank food basket distribution,“Cesta Basica”, for people affected by COVID-19
GOVERNMENT PARTNERS
State Secretariat for Civil Protection
Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries
Ministry of Health
National Logistics Centre
Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs
Ministry of Tourism, Commerce and Industry
